edbDesc: Generation of electrical pulses when a specially processed wire is moved in a magnetic field. The wire has two distinct magnetic regions that react differently to the magnetic field: the shell requires a strong magnetic field to reverse its magnetic polarity, whereas the core will revert under weaker field conditions. The polarity of the wire shifts very rapidly, generating strong, short (~10 µs) electrical pulses without additional external power.
title: Wiegand effect
description: A specially twisted wire flips its magnetism all at once as a magnet passes, giving off a sharp electric pulse no matter how slowly the magnet moves. Wiegand patented the wire in the 1970s, and it powers battery-free rotation counters and the classic Wiegand access-card readers.
effect: a treated wire flips its magnetism suddenly and gives a sharp pulse
usedIn: Pulse counters in water and gas meters
strength: Each flip gives a pulse of a few volts in a small coil, enough to power a counter chip for an instant with no battery.
pickWhy: Specific named effect that detects motion and harvests energy; date is the 1974 patent, approximately.
